summary: Well-executed, preregistered paired study evaluating a verifier-guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline for LLM→network-configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Execution artifacts are archived and sampling/paired design are transparent. Results show very high baseline compliance (199/200) and a single guarded repair improvement (200/200); effect size is tiny and not statistically significant given one discordant pair. Main limitations are synthetic tasks, single model, and shared_initial_candidate semantics which constrain the estimand to verifier/repair effect only.
required_revisions: Replace any DOI/arXiv/identifier-only reference entries in the References section with full conventional IEEE-formatted bibliography entries (authors, title, venue, year, DOI/URL as supplementary). Ensure the manuscript's numbered citations [1], [2], ... map to those full IEEE entries. This is required by the track and verifier guidance and can be resolved from the archived verified-reference records.

For every numbered citation used to support a specific scholarly claim in the prose, add or confirm a short parenthetical or inline clarifier (in the nearest sentence or footnote) tying that claim to the cited work's actual contribution (e.g., “prototype intent→config pipelines [2]”, “generate→validate→repair pattern demonstrated in program-repair contexts [4]”). This ensures citation semantics (that the cited work actually supports the nearby claim) and can be resolved from the verified bibliography artifacts.
optional_revisions: Condense the Disclosure Statement so it remains complete but avoids repeating execution-log-level accounting already present in the archived manifest; retain the mandatory master-prompt locator + SHA-256 verbatim.

In Results or Methods, briefly note the practical implications of the observed extremely high baseline pass rate for the preregistered power calculation (e.g., show the post-hoc detectable minimum effect size given observed discordant counts), to help readers interpret the null statistical result.

Consider adding, in Limitations or Future Work, an explicit recommendation that future runs use independent first-pass generation (not shared_initial_candidate) when the scientific question is to measure generation/constraint effects rather than verifier/repair effects.
